questions.title: Gateway API: header match + weighted split
questions.question:
ssh cka03010
In namespace shop-gw a Gateway shop-gw (HTTP, port 80) and Services shop-v1 and shop-v2 exist.
Create an HTTPRoute named shop-route attached to shop-gw for hostname shop.example.com:
- Requests with header x-version: v2 go 100% to shop-v2.
- All other requests are split 80% shop-v1 and 20% shop-v2.
Both Services listen on port 80.
questions.setup:
kubectl get crd gateways.gateway.networking.k8s.io >/dev/null 2>&1 || kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/download/v1.2.1/standard-install.yaml
kubectl create namespace shop-gw --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: GatewayClass
metadata: {name: cka-demo}
spec: {controllerName: example.net/gateway-controller}
---
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata: {name: shop-gw, namespace: shop-gw}
spec:
  gatewayClassName: cka-demo
  listeners: [{name: http, protocol: HTTP, port: 80}]
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: shop-v1, namespace: shop-gw}
spec: {selector: {app: shop, v: "1"}, ports: [{port: 80}]}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: shop-v2, namespace: shop-gw}
spec: {selector: {app: shop, v: "2"}, ports: [{port: 80}]}
EOF
questions.meaning: Send testers (header v2) to version 2 and split everyone else 80/20.
questions.words:
• Gateway = the entry point that listens (HTTP port 80)
  • GatewayClass = which controller runs it
  • HTTPRoute = routing rules attached to a Gateway
  • parentRefs = which Gateway
  • backendRefs = which Services get the traffic

flow.t: kubectl -n shop-gw get gateway shop-gw -o yaml | grep -A3 listeners

flow.h: Route will attach to this.

flow.t:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/route.yaml
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata: {name: shop-route, namespace: shop-gw}
spec:
  parentRefs: [{name: shop-gw}]
  hostnames: [shop.example.com]
  rules:
  - matches:
    - headers: [{name: x-version, value: v2}]
    backendRefs: [{name: shop-v2, port: 80}]
  - matches:
    - path: {type: PathPrefix, value: /}
    backendRefs:
    - {name: shop-v1, port: 80, weight: 80}
    - {name: shop-v2, port: 80, weight: 20}
EOF

flow.h: cat <<'EOF' > /root/route.yaml ... EOF starts a "heredoc". It writes every line up to EOF into /root/route.yaml. This is the same as pasting into vim. Rule 1 has no path, so it also matches path /. With equal paths, Gateway API picks the rule with more header matches. So x-version: v2 requests go 100% to shop-v2.

flow.t: kubectl -n shop-gw describe httproute shop-route | grep -A20 Rules

flow.h: Both rules stored correctly. Status stays empty. The playground GatewayClass points to a fake controller. So nothing sets Accepted. Check the spec only.

  - matches:
    - path: {type: PathPrefix, value: /}
    backendRefs:
    - {name: shop-v1, port: 80, weight: 80}
    - {name: shop-v2, port: 80, weight: 20}
EOF
kubectl apply -f /root/route.yaml
kubectl -n shop-gw describe httproute shop-route | grep -A20 Rules
kubectl -n shop-gw get httproute shop-route -o yaml

`backendRefs: - name: shop-v1, port: 80`, because a Service backend needs its port
`weight: 80` and `weight: 20`, because weight is a plain number, not a percent string

questions.title: NetworkPolicy pick: AND vs OR trap
questions.question:
ssh cka03011
Pods labelled app=api in namespace payments must accept traffic ONLY from Pods labelled app=gateway in namespace edge, on TCP port 80. A default deny-ingress policy exists in payments.
Several candidate policies are in /root/netpols-ex/. Apply the single file that meets the requirement with the least privilege. Do not modify any file or existing policy.
questions.meaning: Pick the rule where namespace AND pod label must both match, on port 80 only.
questions.words:
• least privilege = allow only what is needed, nothing more
  • AND = both namespace and pod label must match (one list item)
  • OR = either one is enough (two list items)

flow.t: for f in /root/netpols-ex/*.yaml; do echo "== $f"; cat $f; done

flow.h: for f in ...; do ...; done repeats cat for every file. Each "-" under from: starts a separate OR item. a = OR: every pod in edge, OR app=gateway pods in payments. Alone, podSelector means the policy's own namespace. b = AND + TCP 80. c = right senders but EVERY port. d = all edge pods to all payments pods. b is the only least-privilege match.
One file, no edits.

flow.t: kubectl -n edge exec gateway -- wget -qO- -T2 api.payments | head -2
kubectl -n edge exec intruder -- wget -qO- -T2 api.payments

flow.h: Only the gateway pod gets in. If the intruder is NOT blocked, check the network plugin enforces policies. Run kubectl -n kube-system get pods | grep -E 'calico|canal|cilium'.

questions.mug:
for f in /root/netpols-ex/*.yaml; do echo "== $f"; cat $f; done
kubectl apply -f /root/netpols-ex/b.yaml
kubectl -n edge exec gateway -- wget -qO- -T2 api.payments | head -2
kubectl -n edge exec intruder -- wget -qO- -T2 api.payments
kubectl -n payments get networkpolicy

pic.say: Pick the rule where namespace AND pod label must both match, on port 80 only. Words you need: least privilege = allow only what is needed, nothing more; AND = both namespace and pod label must match (one list item); OR = either one is enough (two list items).

story.broken: Guard rule sheets look alike; one wrongly lets in any edge pod OR any gateway pod.
story.fix: Apply the policy with namespace AND pod selector in one from item, plus port 80.

coach.pattern: Pick the least-privilege NetworkPolicy: AND vs OR selectors

clues.q: ONLY from Pods labelled app=gateway in namespace edge
clues.means: Need namespaceSelector AND podSelector in the SAME from item
Exactly one k apply; don't edit files

traps.dont: Pick a file with `- namespaceSelector` and `- podSelector` as two items
traps.do: Pick the file with one item holding both selectors, because two items mean OR

traps.dont: Pick a file with no `ports:` block
traps.do: `k apply -f /root/netpols-ex/b.yaml`, because it also limits traffic to TCP port 80 (least privilege)

questions.question:
ssh cka03012
In namespace dns-lab, Deployment catalog (2 replicas, nginx on port 80) exists.
- Expose it with a ClusterIP Service catalog-svc on port 8080 targeting port 80.
- Create a headless Service catalog-headless for the same Pods on port 80.
- From a temporary busybox:1.36 Pod, save the nslookup output of catalog-svc.dns-lab.svc.cluster.local to /root/svc-dns.txt, and of catalog-headless.dns-lab.svc.cluster.local to /root/headless-dns.txt.

questions.meaning: Make a normal and a "headless" service and record what DNS answers for each.
questions.words:
• ClusterIP Service = one fixed virtual IP in front of the pods
  • headless Service (clusterIP = None) = no virtual IP, DNS returns every pod IP
  • DNS A record = a name → IP answer

flow.t: kubectl -n dns-lab rollout status deploy catalog

questions.title: HPA: CPU + memory, scaleUp and scaleDown behavior
questions.question:
ssh cka03013
Create a HorizontalPodAutoscaler named worker-hpa in namespace metrics-app for Deployment worker:
- min 2, max 6 replicas,
- target 60% average CPU utilisation AND 70% average memory utilisation,
- scale up by at most 2 Pods per 60 seconds,
- scale-down stabilization window of 120 seconds.
questions.meaning: Autoscale on CPU and memory. Add at most 2 pods a minute. Remove pods only after 2 calm minutes.
questions.words:
• HPA = HorizontalPodAutoscaler, adds/removes pods automatically
  • utilisation = usage ÷ request, in %
  • stabilization window = how long HPA waits before scaling down

flow.t:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/hpa.yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata: {name: worker-hpa, namespace: metrics-app}
spec:
  scaleTargetRef: {apiVersion: apps/v1, kind: Deployment, name: worker}
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 6
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource: {name: cpu, target: {type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 60}}
  - type: Resource
    resource: {name: memory, target: {type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 70}}
  behavior:
    scaleUp:
      policies:
      - {type: Pods, value: 2, periodSeconds: 60}
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 120
EOF

flow.h: cat <<'EOF' > /root/hpa.yaml ... EOF starts a "heredoc". It writes every line up to EOF into /root/hpa.yaml. This is the same as pasting into vim. Two metrics: HPA computes replicas for each and uses the higher. scaleUp policy Pods 2 / 60 s = add at most 2 pods per minute. scaleDown stabilizationWindowSeconds 120 = look back 2 min before removing pods. It acts on the highest recommendation of the last 2 min.

flow.t: cpu: <unknown>/60%, memory: <unknown>/70%   MINPODS 2   MAXPODS 6 (real % instead of <unknown> if metrics-server runs)

flow.h: <unknown> = no metrics (yet); the config is still right.
HPA raises the Deployment to minReplicas even without metrics (it started with 1).

questions.mug:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/hpa.yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata: {name: worker-hpa, namespace: metrics-app}
spec:
  scaleTargetRef: {apiVersion: apps/v1, kind: Deployment, name: worker}
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 6
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource: {name: cpu, target: {type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 60}}
  - type: Resource
    resource: {name: memory, target: {type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 70}}
  behavior:
    scaleUp:
      policies:
      - {type: Pods, value: 2, periodSeconds: 60}
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 120
EOF
kubectl apply -f /root/hpa.yaml
kubectl -n metrics-app get hpa worker-hpa
kubectl -n metrics-app get deploy worker
kubectl -n metrics-app get hpa worker-hpa -o yaml | grep -A12 behavior
questions.docs: kubernetes.io: Horizontal Pod Autoscaling (search: scaling policies behavior scaleUp)

pic.say: Autoscale on CPU and memory. Add at most 2 pods a minute. Remove pods only after 2 calm minutes. Words you need: HPA = HorizontalPodAutoscaler, adds/removes pods automatically; utilisation = usage ÷ request, in %; stabilization window = how long HPA waits before scaling down.

story.broken: Nobody adjusts worker copies when CPU or memory gets busy.
story.fix: HPA worker-hpa: min 2, max 6, CPU 60%, memory 70%, with scaleUp and scaleDown policies.

questions.title: PriorityClass with preemption policy
questions.question:
ssh cka03014
Create a PriorityClass named critical-jobs:
- value exactly one less than the highest existing user-defined PriorityClass (ignore system-*),
- preemptionPolicy PreemptLowerPriority, not the global default,
- description "critical batch".
Patch Deployment payments-api in namespace prio to use it, and verify that the running Pods have the new priority value.
questions.setup:
kubectl create namespace prio --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata: {name: batch-low}
value: 100
---
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata: {name: team-a}
value: 3000
---
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata: {name: team-b}
value: 7000
preemptionPolicy: Never
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: payments-api, namespace: prio}
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: payments-api}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: payments-api}}
    spec:
      priorityClassName: batch-low
      containers: [{name: c, image: nginx:1.27-alpine}]
EOF
questions.meaning: Create a priority just under the top one. Allow it to push others out. Give it to a deployment.
questions.words:
• PriorityClass = a named number, higher = scheduled first
  • preemption = evicting lower-priority pods to make room
  • globalDefault = the class used by pods that name none

flow.t: NAME VALUE header, then lowest → highest: batch-low 100, team-a 3000, team-b 7000 (highest = last line)

flow.h: --sort-by sorts ascending. custom-columns prints only name and value. grep -v system- hides the system-* classes.

flow.t:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/pc.yaml
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata: {name: critical-jobs}
value: 6999
globalDefault: false
preemptionPolicy: PreemptLowerPriority
description: "critical batch"
EOF

flow.h: cat <<'EOF' > /root/pc.yaml ... EOF starts a "heredoc". It writes every line up to EOF into /root/pc.yaml. This is the same as pasting into vim. PreemptLowerPriority (the default) = may evict lower-priority pods to make room. Do NOT copy Never from team-b.
Replaces batch-low; changing the pod template starts a rollout.

flow.t: kubectl -n prio rollout status deploy payments-api

flow.h: Priority is copied into each new pod.

questions.mug:
kubectl get pc --sort-by=.value -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,VALUE:.value | grep -v system-
cat <<'EOF' > /root/pc.yaml
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata: {name: critical-jobs}
value: 6999
globalDefault: false
preemptionPolicy: PreemptLowerPriority
description: "critical batch"
EOF
kubectl apply -f /root/pc.yaml
kubectl -n prio patch deploy payments-api -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"priorityClassName":"critical-jobs"}}}}'
kubectl -n prio rollout status deploy payments-api
kubectl -n prio get pods -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,PRIO:.spec.priority,CLASS:.spec.priorityClassName
kubectl get pc critical-jobs -o yaml | grep -E "value|preemption|globalDefault"

story.fix: PriorityClass critical-jobs (highest minus 1, PreemptLowerPriority); patch the Deployment to use it.

questions.title: StorageClass (Retain, expandable) + StatefulSet claims
questions.question:
ssh cka03015
Create a StorageClass named retain-local: provisioner rancher.io/local-path, reclaimPolicy Retain, volumeBindingMode WaitForFirstConsumer, allowVolumeExpansion true. It must NOT be the default.
In namespace cache create a StatefulSet cache (2 replicas, image redis:7-alpine, headless Service cache) with a volumeClaimTemplate named data requesting 100Mi from retain-local, mounted at /data.
keys: sc = retain-local (Retain, WFFC, expandable, not default)
questions.setup:
kubectl get deploy -A | grep -q local-path-provisioner || kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rancher/local-path-provisioner/v0.0.30/deploy/local-path-storage.yaml
kubectl create namespace cache --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
questions.meaning: Make a storage type that keeps disks after delete. Make a 2-pod database that gets one disk each.
questions.words:
• StatefulSet = pods with stable names (cache-0, cache-1) and one disk each
  • headless Service = gives those pods DNS names
  • volumeClaimTemplates = the PVC pattern copied per pod
  • reclaimPolicy Retain = keep the disk after its claim is deleted

flow.t:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/sc.yaml
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata: {name: retain-local}
provisioner: rancher.io/local-path
reclaimPolicy: Retain
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
allowVolumeExpansion: true
EOF

flow.h: cat <<'EOF' > /root/sc.yaml ... EOF starts a "heredoc". It writes every line up to EOF into /root/sc.yaml. This is the same as pasting into vim. No default annotation = not default.
Each replica gets its own PVC, named <template>-<statefulset>-<number> = data-cache-0, data-cache-1.

flow.t: cache-0 then cache-1 Running (they start one after another; wait for the redis pull); data-cache-0 / data-cache-1 Bound; RECLAIM Retain

flow.h: PVs keep the Retain policy.

questions.mug:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/sc.yaml
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata: {name: retain-local}
provisioner: rancher.io/local-path
reclaimPolicy: Retain
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
allowVolumeExpansion: true
EOF
kubectl apply -f /root/sc.yaml
cat <<'EOF' > /root/sts.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: cache, namespace: cache}
spec: {clusterIP: None, selector: {app: cache}, ports: [{port: 6379}]}
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata: {name: cache, namespace: cache}
spec:
  serviceName: cache
  replicas: 2
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: cache}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: cache}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - {name: redis, image: redis:7-alpine, volumeMounts: [{name: data, mountPath: /data}]}
  volumeClaimTemplates:
  - metadata: {name: data}
    spec:
      accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
      storageClassName: retain-local
      resources: {requests: {storage: 100Mi}}
EOF
kubectl apply -f /root/sts.yaml
kubectl -n cache get pods,pvc
kubectl get pv | grep retain-local
kubectl get sc retain-local
kubectl -n cache get pvc

questions.title: Re-bind a Released PV (clear claimRef)
questions.question:
ssh cka03016
The PostgreSQL data PersistentVolume pg-data-pv still holds data, but it is in Released state after its old claim was deleted.
- Make the PV available again WITHOUT deleting it or its data.
- Create PVC pg-data in namespace postgres (1Gi, ReadWriteOnce, storageClassName manual) that binds to it.
- Deploy /root/pg-deploy.yaml (already uses claim pg-data) and make sure the Pod is Running.
questions.meaning: An old disk is "locked" to a deleted claim. Unlock it, claim it again, and start the database.
questions.words:
• Released = old claim gone, but the PV is still reserved for it
  • claimRef = that reservation inside the PV
  • reclaimPolicy Retain = the disk and data are kept when the claim is deleted

flow.h: Released PVs never bind again by themselves.
The --type=json patch {"op":"remove","path":"/spec/claimRef"} deletes the claimRef field. Or run kubectl edit pv pg-data-pv and delete the claimRef block. Frees the PV; data stays on disk.
Ready for a new claim. Check this first, so you know the patch worked.

flow.t:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/pvc.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: pg-data, namespace: postgres}
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: manual
  resources: {requests: {storage: 1Gi}}
EOF

flow.h: cat <<'EOF' > /root/pvc.yaml ... EOF starts a "heredoc". It writes every line up to EOF into /root/pvc.yaml. This is the same as pasting into vim. Class + size + mode match the PV.

flow.t: Bound pg-data-pv / Running (ContainerCreating for ~1 min while postgres:17-alpine downloads)

flow.h: Database runs on the old disk.

apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: pg-data, namespace: postgres}
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: manual
  resources: {requests: {storage: 1Gi}}
EOF
kubectl apply -f /root/pvc.yaml
kubectl apply -f /root/pg-deploy.yaml

traps.dont: `k delete pv pg-data-pv` and recreate it
traps.do: `k patch pv pg-data-pv --type=json -p='[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/claimRef"}]'`, which frees it and keeps the data

traps.dont: Create the PVC without checking the patch worked
traps.do: `k get pv pg-data-pv` must show Available first, so you know the patch worked

traps.dont: Create PVC pg-data in namespace default
traps.do: Set `namespace: postgres` on PVC pg-data. A Pod can only use claims in its own namespace.

memorise: cat <<'EOF' > /root/pvc.yaml: pg-data, ns postgres, RWO, manual, 1Gi → k apply -f /root/pvc.yaml
k apply -f /root/pg-deploy.yaml; k -n postgres get pvc,pods
